_about: The repository's worked example of story element continuity: six spreads of the same three people as the rest of the examples, as records. A spread has no number here; its place is in editions/*.json. Names are tokens; the pictures in art/ are placeholders named after their spreads; parked-art.json accounts for every picture nothing loads; built/ is output written by node scripts/story.mjs build examples/story and never edited.
title: Six Hours

triptych.about: three pictures in a row above the text

the-porch.title: The porch
paragraphs: {{chloe-jenkins}} dug through her bag for her keys while {{sam-hayes}} read the message again under the porch bulb. It was the fourth time since the cab.
Six hours. He had opened it at 11:52 and said nothing. {{sam-hayes}} knew the minute the way you know a birthday.

dialogue.speaker: {{sam-hayes}}
dialogue.text: He read it. Look, it says read.

the-porch.margin_note: I counted the hours like they were evidence. They were not evidence. They were hours.
the-porch.picture: Two women on a narrow front porch at night, one bent over a glowing phone, one at the door with her keys out.

read-at-1152.title: Read at 11:52
paragraphs: At the kitchen table {{sam-hayes:formal}} laid the phone face up between the mugs, like a card she had been dealt and could not put down.
{{theo-vance:full}} signed his contracts with his whole name. He signed her with one letter.

dialogue.speaker: {{chloe-jenkins}}
dialogue.text: It is a text. Read me what it says.

read-at-1152.margin_note: One letter can hold a whole person, or hide one. I did not know yet which.
read-at-1152.footnote: A read receipt says a screen was open. It does not say a person was ready.
read-at-1152.picture: {{sam-hayes:full}} at a kitchen table under lamplight, {{cracked-phone}} glowing between two mugs, {{chloe-jenkins}} across from her.

the-napkin-timeline.title: The napkin timeline
paragraphs: {{chloe-jenkins}} drew the evening on a napkin: the message at 5:40, the read at 11:52, the long flat line between them.
{{sam-hayes}} looked at the line as if it might say something the phone had not.
the-napkin-timeline.picture: A paper napkin on a kitchen table with a timeline drawn in pen, two pairs of hands at its edges.

across-town.title: Across town
paragraphs: Across town {{theo-vance}} turned his phone face down on the workbench and picked up the plane again. The board did not need planing.
On its nail by the door hung {{brass-key}}, where it always hung. He had not locked up. He was not leaving yet.
across-town.margin_note: I was not ignoring her. I was ignoring the part of me that wanted to answer.
across-town.picture: A man alone in a carpenter's workshop under a hanging bulb, a phone face down beside the plane, a brass key on a nail by the door.

morning-at-the-workbench.title: Morning at the workbench
paragraphs: At six {{theo-vance}} wrote a reply, read it twice, and deleted it. Then he wrote a shorter one and deleted that.
He took {{brass-key}} off its nail and locked the shop behind him, which he had never once forgotten to do.
morning-at-the-workbench.margin_note: Deleting a sentence felt safer than sending one. It was not safer. It was just quieter.
morning-at-the-workbench.picture: {{theo-vance}} in the workshop doorway at dawn, {{brass-key}} in his hand, grey light on the sawdust.

the-text-sent.title: The text, sent
paragraphs: {{sam-hayes}} typed it on the porch where she had read his, so the two messages would at least share a place.
Nine miles away a phone turned face up on a workbench. {{theo-vance}} read it standing, the way he read invoices.

dialogue.speaker: {{sam-hayes}}
dialogue.text: I'd like to know where I stand. You can tell me tonight, or you can tell me now.

the-text-sent.margin_note: I sent the thing I was afraid of. The fear came along. It did not get to drive.
the-text-sent.footnote: Saying where you stand is not a demand. It is a map with your own position marked on it.
the-text-sent.picture: Three pictures in a row: a thumb over the send button of a cracked phone; the sent message alone on a screen; {{theo-vance}} reading it standing at the workbench.
